analyst_view.overall: Early view: Feyenoord host Excelsior in the Rotterdam derby after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen, five games without a win and top spot gone; Giovanni van Bronckhorst says this one must be won. Porto visit De Kuip in the Champions League three days later. Excelsior have lost five league games in a row, including 0-9 to Twente, though the 0-1 against Go Ahead Eagles was closer.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals. Feyenoord should score, but goalkeeper Tjark Ernst is conceding more than expected by Opta's numbers and Excelsior have not scored in two games, so the home side carries almost all of it. I agree with the total rather than move it.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I lean higher: after the 0-9 at Twente Excelsior's priority under Ruben den Uil will be a compact low block, and a Feyenoord side desperate for a win will pile on crosses and blocked shots.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. It is a derby, Excelsior will defend deep and foul to stop counters, and Feyenoord are under pressure after five games without a win, which tends to bring rash challenges and protests. I lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots with 19 for Feyenoord. That matches a one-sided game against a team defending deep, and the Porto game three days later could see some rotation that stops it climbing further.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Excelsior's 3.1 looks generous for a team that has gone two games without scoring, and a packed defence blocks many of Feyenoord's attempts.
